newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crudes steady to lower, Brent/Dubai narrows.
newsitem.headline: Asian crudes steady to lower, Brent/Dubai narrows.

text.p: Asian crude oil prices were flat to slightly lower on Monday in a market deprived of direction from London, closed for a U.K. national holiday.
The Brent/Dubai narrowed further amid a steady Dubai but weakening Brent market.
October Brent/Dubai was talked $1.62/$1.78, although one trader was offering earlier in the day at $1.82. That compared with $1.79/$1.85 Friday.
Intermonth Dubai quotes were steady but well bid on Monday with Oct/November at a notional 32/40 cents and Nov/Dec at 32/40.
The Brent futures market was closed on Monday but NYMEX crude, trading on the after-hours ACCESS system, dipped. October was last traded at $21.95, down just one cent from New York.
On the basis of Friday Brent/NYMEX arbitrage value of $1.55 that left October Brent Monday at $20.40 per barrel.
Traders reported little discussion of regional crude grades, with Minas assessed around previous levels done of ICP minus 25 cents.
China was said to have acquired 400,000 barrels of Minas Friday at ICP minus 29 cents.
Middle East grades continued to find support.
On Friday, a U.S. major bought an October Dubai cargo from a European major at full-month quotes plus 52 cents, up from the previous deal done of full-month quotes plus 47 cents.
The same U.S. major bought a Murban cargo Friday at ADNOC plus 15, one cent lower than a cargo it had acquired Thursday.
The same major bought an October Oman cargo from another U.S. major of Friday at MPM plus 2.5 cents, shaving one half a cent off previous October deals.
Traders said another package cargo of late September Lower Zakum and October Umm Shaif may have been traded Friday.
